chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed to a prophet among the prophets, while he was in the dominion of a tyrant among the tyrants: 'Go to this tyrant and say to him: I did not appoint you for the shedding of blood and the taking of wealth, but I appointed you only to keep the cries of the oppressed away from Me. For I will not overlook their oppression, even if they are disbelievers.'
ai.seo_question: What is the primary purpose of a ruler's authority according to divine revelation in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-A'mal* elucidates the teleology of political authority in Shia thought, distinguishing between the ruler's utilitarian role in maintaining order and the divine imperative to protect the vulnerable. It underscores the concept of *Adl* (justice) as an objective standard, where the ruler’s legitimacy is contingent upon his ability to curb the cries of the oppressed, regardless of their faith. This narrative reinforces the principle that divine accountability extends to the political sphere, making the cessation of oppression a primary criterion for righteous governance.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 4. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakil who said it was narrated to me by Abdillah b. Ja’far from Muhammad b. al-Hussain from al-Hassan b. Mahbub from Ishaq b. Ammar from Abi Abdillah (a.s.)

who said: Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s.) relates that the ruler of the time of a prophet was unjust. The Almighty Allah revealed on His prophet, “Go and tell your ruler that he is not being made the ruler to oppress people. He is made the ruler to stop injustice to the people. Surely I am not going to forgive the injustice done to the subjects even if they are disbelievers.”
